categories.main_business_segments: Gakken Holdings operates primarily in two main business segments: the Education segment and the Medical & Welfare segment. The Education segment includes classroom and cram school operations, publishing and content distribution, and products and services for kindergartens and schools. The Medical & Welfare segment encompasses the planning, development, and operation of senior housing, dementia group homes, and child-rearing support facilities. There is also an 'Other' segment, which includes logistics and specialized group services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages expertise in educational content development, digital and print publishing, and the operation of educational and welfare facilities. Production methods include in-house content creation, digital transformation (DX) initiatives, and the use of proprietary assessment and learning management systems. In the welfare segment, facility operation is supported by standardized processes and efficiency improvements, while sustainability initiatives such as energy-efficient buildings and resource recycling are being implemented.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include children (from preschool to high school), parents, educational institutions, teachers, and healthcare/welfare service users such as seniors and families. The company serves the education market (cram schools, schools, kindergartens, and publishers), the healthcare and eldercare market (senior housing, group homes), and the child-rearing support market (nurseries, after-school care). Corporate clients are also served through training and e-learning solutions.
categories.geographic_coverage: Gakken's operations are primarily based in Japan, with a nationwide presence in both education and welfare facilities. The company also has a growing international footprint, particularly in Asia (notably Vietnam and other Southeast Asian countries), through subsidiaries and acquisitions. Over 90% of sales and assets are concentrated in Japan, but overseas expansion is a strategic focus.
categories.supply_chain_position: Gakken operates downstream in the supply chain, directly providing educational services, published content, and welfare/childcare services to end users. The company also engages in midstream activities through the development and distribution of educational materials and content to schools and other institutions. Logistics and group support services further integrate the supply chain internally.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding global business, investing in recurrent and reskilling education, and growing the medical/wellness business. The company emphasizes high value-added services, digital transformation, and sustainability (ESG/SDGs). R&D is focused on digital content, e-learning, and innovative educational and welfare solutions, with ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency and develop new business models.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through service fees (tuition for cram schools, facility usage fees for welfare/childcare), product sales (books, educational materials, supplies), and content licensing. Additional income streams include corporate training, e-learning subscriptions, and logistics services. The company also earns rental income from real estate and receives dividends from subsidiaries.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other large education service providers (e.g., Benesse, Z-kai), publishing companies, and eldercare operators. Gakken is positioned as a leading integrated provider in both education and welfare, with a strong brand and diversified portfolio. The company is among the top players in the Japanese education and senior care markets, with a growing presence in digital and international segments.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending September 2025, consolidated sales reached 199.1 billion yen (up 7.3% year-on-year), with operating profit of 8.2 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 3.6 billion yen. The company employs over 10,000 people (over 19,000 including temporary staff). Gakken has demonstrated steady growth in both revenue and profit, with a strategic target of 205 billion yen in sales and 8.5 billion yen in net profit by FY2026.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Gakken emphasizes its ability to deliver high-quality, comprehensive educational and welfare solutions that address societal needs such as lifelong learning, child development, and aging populations. The company differentiates itself through its integrated approach, combining content, services, and facility operation, as well as its commitment to sustainability, digital innovation, and social value creation. Its strong brand, extensive network, and focus on high value-added, differentiated services are key competitive advantages.
